rdf:Description.dc:title: Commissioners for the District of Columbia
rdf:Description.dc:description: In 1791, President Washington appointed Thomas Johnson, Daniel Carroll, and David Stuart commissioners to supervise the planning, design, and construction of the new capital city and surrounding federal district. They oversaw the survey and land acquisition of the district, and were responsible for approving a modified version of Pierre Charles L'Enfant's city plan.
